title: Runtime weekly sync — scratch agenda (Tyra)
content:
Meeting date: 2026-03-13 (weekly runtime sync)
Owner: Tyra Chen — casual notes / prep scratchpad
Goal for this week: quick alignment on regressions, short-term ops, and a single small deep dive on KV cache eviction tuning so we have a clear action plan going into the sprint review. Keep meeting <= 45m.

Quick snapshot to paste in Slack before standup: 
 - 2 major perf anomalies open (ENGINF-4123, ENGINF-4198) — see notes below
 - Autoscaling observed backpressure on 2x-midnight spike (Thu/ Fri) — investigating
 - Console tracing rollout for model-pin is ~50% complete, plan to flip feature flag next Tue if no regressions

Agenda (high level, timeboxed):
 1) 5m — Quick wins / shoutouts (on-call rotations, ops docs updated)
 2) 10m — Incident follow-up: ENGINF-4123 (kernel memory regression) — Miguel
 3) 10m — Autoscale backpressure observations + short mitigations options — Priya
 4) 15m — Deep dive: KV cache eviction policy tuning proposal (proposal + perf table) — Tyra
 5) 5m — Action items & owners / next checks

Notes to self / Things to pull before meeting:
 - Perf graphs: 99th latency and memory by model variant (pull from console last 14d)
 - Link to PR 980 (kernel fix) and the benchmark run logs — include critical diff lines
 - Small table: baseline throughput (tokens/s) vs quantized path — need to show impact of eviction frequency on tail latency
 - Check recent rollout metrics for model-pin feature-flag (console route: /rollouts/model-pin)

Open items (context):
 - ENGINF-4123: regression in kernel selection at seq_len=2048 -> ~6% increase in p99 on T4 nodes after PR #978. Initial bisect points to a change in the scheduling heuristic. Miguel owns next repro steps.
 - ENGINF-4198: sporadic KV cache degenerations causing repeated KV reloads on heavy chat workloads; root cause unclear — hypothesis: rare tag mismatch + LRU edge-case. Priya to attach memprof traces.
 - Autoscale backpressure: observed during 02:00 PST burst — autoscaler did not create new replicas fast enough for a sustained 90s burst; suggests tuning of scale-up thresholds for request queue depth.

Deep dive: KV cache eviction tuning (draft notes)\ - Problem: current eviction window (90s) tuned for average request flow, but bursts cause cache misses that amplify token generation latency when multiple concurrent requests trigger full KV reloads.\ - Hypothesis: shorter eviction + small adaptive prefetch reduces tail latency for chat workloads with short-lived prefixes; tradeoff is slightly higher memory churn and occasional stale keys.\ - Proposal (concrete):
   * Add adaptive TTL: base_ttl=45s, extend on repeated hits per prefix (>3 hits in 30s) to 3x base_ttl
   * Add a soft-prefetch for top-3 upcoming token positions when a request queue length > 8
   * Instrument counters: eviction_count, prefetch_count, kv_reload_latency (millis) and a per-prefix hit-rate metric
 - Expected outcome: reduce KV reload spikes -> lower p99 by ~15% on chat-heavy traces (back-of-envelope from local sim)
 - Risks: memory increase during high-concurrency; need to verify no cross-customer bleed in Dedicated pools; coordinate with SRE for memory alerts

Action items (tracking) — keep these compact, update status each week:
 - [ ] Miguel Rivera — reproduce ENGINF-4123 on staging & capture kernel scheduler trace — due 2026-03-15 — (status: in_progress)
 - [ ] Priya Singh — attach memprof traces for ENGINF-4198 and upload to PR/issue — due 2026-03-14 — (status: in_progress)
 - [ ] Tyra Chen — prototype adaptive TTL + prefetch in sandbox branch and run 1k-conversation sim — due 2026-03-18 — (status: todo)
 - [ ] Arjun Patel — add perf dashboards for eviction_count and kv_reload_latency (console) — due 2026-03-16 — (status: todo)
 - [ ] On-call (week of 3/15) — add a small runbook note for autoscale emergency scale-up (who pings infra-sig) — due 2026-03-14 — (status: todo)

Parking lot / topics for later weeks:
 - Revisit kernel scheduling heuristic refactor (needs design doc) — bump to next retro if regressions continue
 - Dedicated capacity memory isolation tests — coordinate with Private team for on-prem proposals

Meeting cadence notes / housekeeping:
 - Try 45m cap; timebox deep dives to 15m and follow up asynchronously for design docs
 - If item is purely ops (alerts, runbook edits) move to SRE weekly unless owners request platform attention
 - Quick thumbs-up culture: send the short Slack recap after the meeting with bullet action items and owners

Quick draft Slack summary I will paste after the sync:
 "Runtime sync done: Miguel reproducing kernel-regression (ENGINF-4123), Priya collecting memprof for KV issue (ENGINF-4198), Tyra prototyping adaptive-KV TTL; Arjun to add eviction telemetry. Action items assigned — see pinned doc. Next check: Tue 3/16 for PR smoke test results."

Notes-to-self: keep this doc pared down. Move final agenda to shared drive or post as thread in #eng-runtime before meeting. If someone wants to deep dive, create a separate design doc and link it (avoid long text in weekly notes).

End of scratchpad.
